theorem fieldOneFiniteStageSoninExponentCoefficient_subset
    (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum ℤ)) (A : Finset ↥S) :

source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem fieldOneFiniteStageSoninExponentCoefficient_subset
    (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum ℤ)) (A : Finset ↥S) :
    fieldOneFiniteStageSoninExponentCoefficient S
        (fieldOneSoninExponentOfSubset A) =
      fieldOneFiniteStageSoninSubsetCoefficient A
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  classical
  unfold fieldOneFiniteStageSoninExponentCoefficient
  unfold fieldOneFiniteStageSoninSubsetCoefficient
  calc
    (∏ v : ↥S, if fieldOneSoninExponentOfSubset A v = 0 then 1
      else if fieldOneSoninExponentOfSubset A v = -1 then
        -((Rat.HeightOneSpectrum.primesEquiv v.1 : ℂ)⁻¹) else 0) =
        ∏ v ∈ A, (if fieldOneSoninExponentOfSubset A v = 0 then 1
          else if fieldOneSoninExponentOfSubset A v = -1 then
            -((Rat.HeightOneSpectrum.primesEquiv v.1 : ℂ)⁻¹) else 0) := by
      symm
      apply Finset.prod_subset (Finset.subset_univ A)
      intro v hvuniv hvA
      simp [fieldOneSoninExponentOfSubset, hvA]
    _ = ∏ v ∈ A,
        -((Rat.HeightOneSpectrum.primesEquiv v.1 : ℂ)⁻¹) := by
      apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
      intro v hvA
      simp [fieldOneSoninExponentOfSubset, hvA]

`HTGeometry/DyadicReflectionJetLaw.lean` formalizes `(14)`--`(15)` for an arbitrary function, in both

## Lean progress — Pong's independence conclusion, with its hypothesis discharged for every phase

`GaloisForLFunctions/HTGeometry/HelsonPhaseTailIndependence.lean` (wired, axiom-clean):

    recurringCoefficientPatternsSpan_const :
      a single source with constant coefficient displays one pattern, at every prime, so it spans
    tailCoefficientIndependent_shiftJet_const
    tailCoefficientIndependent_phaseShiftJet :
      **a nowhere-vanishing phase keeps the shift--jet palette tail independent**
    tailCoefficientIndependent_helsonShiftJet :
      in particular a unimodular phase does, at every prime-power layer
    primePowerCoefficientShiftedRotatedJet_tailIndependent_phase :
      the same for the rotated clock
    primePowerCoefficientShiftedJets_algebraicIndependent_phase :
      **the complete shifted-jet rectangle of a nowhere-vanishing phase, across a finite window of
      valuation layers, is algebraically independent over the finite-prime rational coefficient
      field**

The obstacle was that the corpus's criterion for tail independence, `RecurringCoefficientPatternsSpan`,
is designed for coefficient families of **finite range**, and a generic Helson phase has infinite
range — no value of `χ(p)` need recur at all, so the criterion is not merely hard to check, it is
false as stated for a generic phase.

It does not have to be checked.  A single source contributes its coefficient as one **common weight**
on every column of the shift--jet rectangle, and `tailCoefficientIndependent_commonWeight_iff` says a
common nowhere-vanishing weight is invisible to tail independence.  So the criterion is applied once,
to the constant family — whose single pattern recurs at every prime — and the phase is then
reinstated as a weight.  Unimodularity enters only through `χ(p) ≠ 0`.

This is the conclusion of Pong's Theorem 5.9 in the form the card consumes, for one source per
valuation layer, with no hypothesis on the arithmetic of the phase.  What remains to reach the
card's `L_χ` statement is the descent from the prime-power palette to the shifted derivatives of
`Z_χ` itself.

theorem slg_bootstrap (h : IsSLGSolution ρ Q u) {Dr dev : ℕ → ℝ} {N₀ : ℕ}
    (hρ : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 0 < ρ n) (hQ : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 0 < Q n)
    (hQρ : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → Q n ≤ ρ n)
    (hdev : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → |slgAbelDrift ρ Q n - Dr n| ≤ dev n)
    (hdev0 : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 0 ≤ dev n)
    (hbdry : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 2 * |Dr n| ≤ 1 / 8)
    (hsum : ∀ K, ∑ k ∈ Finset.Ico N₀ K,
        (2 * |Dr (k + 1) - Dr k| + 2 * (slgControl ρ Q (k + 1) + 2 * dev (k + 1))) ≤ 1 / 8)
    {m : ℕ} (hm : N₀ ≤ m) :
    slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u m
      ≤ 2 * max (slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u N₀) (slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u (N₀ + 1))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem slg_bootstrap (h : IsSLGSolution ρ Q u) {Dr dev : ℕ → ℝ} {N₀ : ℕ}
    (hρ : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 0 < ρ n) (hQ : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 0 < Q n)
    (hQρ : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → Q n ≤ ρ n)
    (hdev : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → |slgAbelDrift ρ Q n - Dr n| ≤ dev n)
    (hdev0 : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 0 ≤ dev n)
    (hbdry : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 2 * |Dr n| ≤ 1 / 8)
    (hsum : ∀ K, ∑ k ∈ Finset.Ico N₀ K,
        (2 * |Dr (k + 1) - Dr k| + 2 * (slgControl ρ Q (k + 1) + 2 * dev (k + 1))) ≤ 1 / 8)
    {m : ℕ} (hm : N₀ ≤ m) :
    slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u m
      ≤ 2 * max (slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u N₀) (slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u (N₀ + 1))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hWpos : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 0 < slgWeight ρ Q n := fun n hn => mul_pos (hρ n hn) (hQ n hn)
  have hF0 : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → 0 ≤ slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u n := fun n hn =>
    slgNormalizedEnergy_nonneg (hρ n hn) (hQ n hn).le (by linarith [hQρ n hn, hρ n hn])
  have hPF : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → |slgPrimitive ρ u n| ≤ 4 * slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u n := fun n hn =>
    abs_slgPrimitive_le (hρ n hn) (hQ n hn).le (hQρ n hn) (hWpos n hn)
  refine abstract_energy_bootstrap
    (F := slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u) (P := slgPrimitive ρ u) (Dr := Dr)
    (ctrl := fun k => slgControl ρ Q (k + 1) + 2 * dev (k + 1)) hF0 hPF (fun k hk => ?_)
    (fun k hk => by
      have := slgControl_nonneg (ρ := ρ) (Q := Q) (n := k + 1) (hρ _ (by omega))
        (hQ _ (by omega)).le
      have := hdev0 (k + 1) (by omega)
      linarith)
    hbdry hsum hm
  have hk1 : N₀ ≤ k + 1 := by omega
  have hk2 : N₀ ≤ k + 2 := by omega
  have htail := slg_increment_tail_bound h (n := k + 1) (hρ _ hk1) (hQ _ hk1).le (hQρ _ hk1)
    (hWpos _ hk1) (hWpos _ hk2)
  have hvir := slgVirial_succ h k
  have hrw : slgDrift ρ Q (k + 1) * (slgVirial ρ Q u (k + 1) / 2)
      = slgAbelDrift ρ Q (k + 1) * (slgPrimitive ρ u (k + 1) - slgPrimitive ρ u k) / 2 := by
    rw [hvir, slgAbelDrift]
    ring
  rw [hrw] at htail
  have hextra : |(slgAbelDrift ρ Q (k + 1) - Dr (k + 1))
        * (slgPrimitive ρ u (k + 1) - slgPrimitive ρ u k) / 2|
      ≤ 2 * dev (k + 1)
        * (slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u k + slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u (k + 1)) := by
    rw [abs_div, abs_of_nonneg (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 2), abs_mul]
    have hp : |slgPrimitive ρ u (k + 1) - slgPrimitive ρ u k|
        ≤ 4 * slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u (k + 1) + 4 * slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u k := by
      refine le_trans (abs_sub _ _) ?_
      linarith [hPF (k + 1) hk1, hPF k hk]
    have hd := hdev (k + 1) hk1
    have hd0 := hdev0 (k + 1) hk1
    have := mul_le_mul hd hp (abs_nonneg _) hd0
    linarith
  have hdecomp : slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u (k + 2) - slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u (k + 1)
      - Dr (k + 1) * (slgPrimitive ρ u (k + 1) - slgPrimitive ρ u k) / 2
      = (slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u (k + 2) - slgNormalizedEnergy ρ Q u (k + 1)
          - slgAbelDrift ρ Q (k + 1)
            * (slgPrimitive ρ u (k + 1) - slgPrimitive ρ u k) / 2)
        + (slgAbelDrift ρ Q (k + 1) - Dr (k + 1))
          * (slgPrimitive ρ u (k + 1) - slgPrimitive ρ u k) / 2 := by ring
  rw [hdecomp]
  refine le_trans (abs_add_le _ _) ?_
  have hFk := hF0 k hk
  have hFk1 := hF0 (k + 1) hk1
  have hc0 := slgControl_nonneg (ρ := ρ) (Q := Q) (n := k + 1) (hρ _ hk1) (hQ _ hk1).le
  nlinarith [htail, hextra, hc0, hFk, hFk1]

    (A : I → Matrix n n ℝ) (B : I → Matrix n m ℝ)

by
  have hle := ccr_numberVariance_le_card_mul_mean A B hcomm hccr
  have heq := ccr_numberVariance_eq_card_mul_mean_iff A B hcomm hccr
  have hC := ccrMixedCommutatorEnergy_nonneg A

  constructor
  · intro hlt
    have hne : ccrNumberVariance A B ≠
        (Fintype.card I : ℝ) * ccrMeanEnergy A := ne_of_lt hlt
    by_cases hC0 : ccrMixedCommutatorEnergy A = 0
    · right
      have hKne : ccrScaledTracelessLeakageEnergy A B ≠ 0 := by
        intro hK0

      exact lt_of_le_of_ne hK (Ne.symm hKne)
    · left
      exact lt_of_le_of_ne hC (Ne.symm hC0)
  · intro hpos
    apply lt_of_le_of_ne hle
    intro hequality
    obtain ⟨hC0, hK0⟩ := heq.mp hequality
    rcases hpos with hCpos | hKpos
    · rw [hC0] at hCpos
      exact (lt_irrefl 0) hCpos
    · rw [hK0] at hKpos

MUST-SOURCE-FIXED-SEPARATORS — Must specify any intermediate separator from source data before treating its energy as an ordering bound. An unspecified maximum along an unknown order gives no independent control. Must retain the signed mixed products when operations are represented by an affine family of fields. Must distinguish an ordering under predetermined endpoint values from bounds on those values: reducing a long block to its initial, separating and final energies still leaves those source energies to estimate. The [actual affine-field partition and complete subpool orders](../../3-formalized/ccm-fu-quotient-window-orders.md) are closed in Lean without numerical premises; they preserve this distinction after arbitrary retained states.


MUST-CONTROL-INHERITED-NONEMPTY-ENERGY — Must control every retained component before its squared mass exceeds the intended total budget. Cannot repair an unbounded lower bound carried by nonempty coordinates using operations that leave those coordinates unchanged, regardless of their available scalar mass. The [uniform child-source floor and scalar-reserve escape theorem](../../5-failed/ccm-fu-increasing-middle-scalar-reserves.md) certify this obstruction analytically in Lean. A surviving energy argument must change those coordinates before the obstruction forms or use another interface.

MUST-PAIR-DIRECTION-WITH-AVAILABILITY — Must prove both directional control and continued availability when corrective operations are supplied by finite source pools. A uniform spanning margin can provide a safe next move, while the smallest remaining pool limits how long that argument continues. Must account for the original squares removed by each merger: their exact cancellation with receiving squares can turn a source pairing into full-energy descent. Cannot infer complete source coverage from arbitrarily long bounded partial orders. The [actual coupled-source cone and growing prime batches](../../3-formalized/ccm-fu-coupled-prime-batches.md) establish this distinction in Lean without numerical premises.

CANNOT-FIXED-FINITE-DIRICHLET-ANNIHILATION — Cannot make one fixed nonzero finite Dirichlet polynomial vanish at every simple critical zeta zero, even after excluding any finite set of ordinates. Must retain nonvanishing at such zeros beyond every height: their unconditional superlinear census exceeds the linear zero budget of every nonzero entire function of finite exponential type. The [finite Dirichlet separation theorem](../../3-formalized/ccm-fu-finite-retained-spectral-separation.md) is closed in Lean with no computational premise. Must separately prove any proposed identity between an arithmetic source integral and the meromorphic expression to which this obstruction is applied.

F688 — [Lean] Coprime deletion insertion has an exact squarefree grading:
`insert_P(a_Q)=a_Q-a_Pa_Q`. On one complete product block, the singleton grade `a_Q` and interaction
grade `a_Pa_Q` are orthogonal for uniform counting, and the insertion energy is exactly `P` times
the dense `Q`-channel energy (`deletionFactorizationInsertion_eq_cofactor_of_coprime`,

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.OneStepKrylovCarrierLaw
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ScalarRecurrenceKrylovReplicaDichotomyLaw

/-!
# First scalar-removed static-Choi Krylov innovation

For a traceless finite Hamiltonian, the first scalar-removed replicated
Krylov load is exactly the replicated directional correlation with its energy
vector.  This removes the inverse Gram matrix at the first nonconstant layer
and is the deterministic input to coefficient-sphere anti-concentration.
-/

open scoped BigOperators ComplexConjugate

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- Removing the identity-Choi component makes the unnormalized spectral
diagonal sum to zero. -/
theorem sum_staticChoiTracelessDiagonal_eq_zero
    {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (energy : Fin d → ℝ)
    (target : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d × Fin d)) :
    ∑ i, staticChoiTracelessDiagonal energy target i = 0 := by
  have h := sum_staticChoiTracelessSpectralCoefficient_eq_zero hd energy target
  have hsqrt : Real.sqrt (d : ℝ) ≠ 0 :=
    ne_of_gt (Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by exact_mod_cast hd))
  rw [show (∑ i, staticChoiTracelessSpectralCoefficient energy target i) =
      ((Real.sqrt (d : ℝ))⁻¹ : ℂ) *
        ∑ i, staticChoiTracelessDiagonal energy target i by
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i hi
    rfl] at h
  exact (mul_eq_zero.mp h).resolve_left (by exact_mod_cast inv_ne_zero hsqrt)

/-- For a traceless spectrum, first scalar-removed carrier mass is exactly
one normalized spectral directional correlation. -/
theorem norm_sq_scalarRemovedStaticChoiKrylovCarrier_one_eq
    {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (energy : Fin d → ℝ)
    (target : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d × Fin d))
    (henergyZero : ∑ i, energy i = 0) :
    ‖spectralKrylovCarrier (fun i => -energy i) 1
        (staticChoiTracelessDiagonal energy target)‖ ^ 2 =
      ‖inner ℂ (spectralPowerVector (fun i => -energy i) 1)
        (staticChoiTracelessDiagonal energy target)‖ ^ 2 /
      ‖spectralPowerVector (fun i => -energy i) 1‖ ^ 2 := by
  apply norm_sq_spectralKrylovCarrier_one_eq_of_sum_zero
  · exact sum_staticChoiTracelessDiagonal_eq_zero hd energy target
  · simpa [Finset.sum_neg_distrib] using congrArg Neg.neg henergyZero

/-- Exact family identity: the order-one replicated carrier load is the sum
of powers of normalized directional correlations. -/
theorem scalarRemovedStaticChoiKrylovReplicaLoad_one_eq
    {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) {W : Type*} [Fintype W]
    (target : W → EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d × Fin d))
    (energy : Fin d → ℝ) (r : ℕ)
    (henergyZero : ∑ i, energy i = 0) :
    scalarRemovedStaticChoiKrylovReplicaLoad target energy 1 r =
      ∑ w, (‖inner ℂ (spectralPowerVector (fun i => -energy i) 1)
          (staticChoiTracelessDiagonal energy (target w))‖ ^ 2 /
        ‖spectralPowerVector (fun i => -energy i) 1‖ ^ 2) ^ r := by
  unfold scalarRemovedStaticChoiKrylovReplicaLoad
    finiteKrylovCarrierReplicaLoad
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro w hw
  rw [pow_mul,
    norm_sq_scalarRemovedStaticChoiKrylovCarrier_one_eq hd energy (target w) henergyZero]

end RHTower

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.BilinearCauchySchwarz
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.DifferencePhaseCurvature
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.DilatedNearDiagonalSum

/-!
# The type-II correlation sums

Pairing the dilation identity `F_{T,r}(m·d) = F_{T,r/m}(d)` with the correlation expansion turns
each off-diagonal term of the type-II energy into a single exponential sum over the LONG variable
`d`, with the difference phase `F_{T,r/m₁} − F_{T,r/m₂}`.  Its curvature scale is
`T(r/m₁ − r/m₂)`, so the abstract curved-phase estimate applies verbatim.
-/

namespace RHTower.Sieve

open Complex RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The unimodular exponential of a phase. -/
def phaseExp (φ : ℝ) : ℂ := Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * φ : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)

theorem phaseExp_mul_conj (φ ψ : ℝ) :
    phaseExp φ * (starRingEnd ℂ) (phaseExp ψ) = phaseExp (φ - ψ) := by
  rw [phaseExp, phaseExp, phaseExp, ← Complex.exp_conj, ← Complex.exp_add]
  congr 1
  rw [map_mul, Complex.conj_I, Complex.conj_ofReal]
  push_cast
  ring

theorem curvedSum_eq_sum_phaseExp (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (A B : ℕ) :
    curvedSum φ A B = ∑ d ∈ Finset.Ico A B, phaseExp (φ d) := rfl

/-- **The correlation sum is a difference-phase sum.** -/
theorem sum_correlation_eq (T r : ℝ) (m₁ m₂ A B : ℕ) :
    (∑ d ∈ Finset.Ico A B,
        phaseExp (nearDiagonalPhase T r ((m₁ : ℝ) * (d : ℝ)))
          * (starRingEnd ℂ) (phaseExp (nearDiagonalPhase T r ((m₂ : ℝ) * (d : ℝ)))))
      = curvedSum (diffPhase T (r / m₁) (r / m₂)) A B := by
  rw [curvedSum_eq_sum_phaseExp]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d _ => ?_
  rw [phaseExp_mul_conj, nearDiagonalPhase_mul T r (m₁ : ℝ) (d : ℝ),
    nearDiagonalPhase_mul T r (m₂ : ℝ) (d : ℝ), diffPhase]

/-- **The off-diagonal correlation bound.** -/
theorem norm_sum_correlation_le {T r : ℝ} (hT : 0 < T) (hr : 0 < r) {m₁ m₂ A B : ℕ}
    (hm₁ : 1 ≤ m₁) (hm : m₁ < m₂) (hA : 1 ≤ A)
    (h4 : 4 * (r / m₁) ≤ (A : ℝ))
    (hlam : curvedLambda (T * (r / m₁ - r / m₂)) (A : ℝ) ≤ 1) :
    ‖∑ d ∈ Finset.Ico A B,
        phaseExp (nearDiagonalPhase T r ((m₁ : ℝ) * (d : ℝ)))
          * (starRingEnd ℂ) (phaseExp (nearDiagonalPhase T r ((m₂ : ℝ) * (d : ℝ))))‖
      ≤ 2500 * Real.sqrt (T * (r / m₁ - r / m₂) / (36 * Real.pi * A))
        + 22 * Real.sqrt (36 * Real.pi / (T * (r / m₁ - r / m₂)))
            * Real.sqrt (((B : ℝ)) ^ 3) := by
  have hm₁0 : (0 : ℝ) < (m₁ : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hm₁
  have hm₂0 : (0 : ℝ) < (m₂ : ℝ) := by
    have : 1 ≤ m₂ := by omega
    exact_mod_cast this
  have hlt : (m₁ : ℝ) < (m₂ : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hm
  have hs₂0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ r / m₂ := by positivity
  have hslt : r / m₂ < r / m₁ := by
    rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ hm₂0 hm₁0]
    nlinarith [hr, hlt]
  rw [sum_correlation_eq]
  exact norm_curvedSum_le_final (curvedPhase_diffPhase hT hs₂0 hslt) A B hA h4 hlam

end

end RHTower.Sieve

/-- The augmented residual is exactly the original regularized remainder, including its constant-coordinate term. -/
theorem residual_eq (v : ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    (∑ j : Option (Deck N), normSq (dir v (source N f e j) (z : ℂ) -
      (slope N f e v z : ℂ) * source N f e j (z : ℂ))) = directionalRemainder N f e v z := by
  rw [Fintype.sum_option, source_none_dir]
  simp only [source, ofComplex_apply, zero_sub, normSq_neg, normSq_mul, normSq_ofReal]
  change slope N f e v z * slope N f e v z * ((e : ℝ) * (e : ℝ)) +
    radialResidual N f v (slope N f e v z) z = _
  unfold directionalRemainder
  ring

/-- The retained remainder is the literal smooth augmented direction energy at every actual source point. -/
theorem directionalRemainder_eq_energy (v : ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    directionalRemainder N f e v z = radius N f e (z : ℂ) ^ 2 *
      ∑ j : Option (Deck N), normSq (dir v (unit N f e j) (z : ℂ)) := by
  rw [← residual_eq, Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  rw [← radius_mul_unit_dir, normSq_mul, normSq_ofReal, ← pow_two]

/-- The complete curvature remainder is the literal two-direction augmented energy. -/
theorem remainder_eq_energy (z : ℍ) :
    remainder N f e z = radius N f e (z : ℂ) ^ 2 *
      ∑ j : Option (Deck N),
        (normSq (dir 1 (unit N f e j) (z : ℂ)) + normSq (dir Complex.I (unit N f e j) (z : ℂ))) := by
  rw [remainder, directionalRemainder_eq_energy, directionalRemainder_eq_energy,
    Finset.sum_add_distrib, mul_add]

/-- Real correlation of the complete augmented directions. -/
def unitCorrelation (z w : ℍ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j : Option (Deck N), (unit N f e j (w : ℂ) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (unit N f e j (z : ℂ))).re

/-- The constant coordinate contributes exactly its positive square to source correlation. -/
theorem correlation_eq_radii_mul (z w : ℍ) :
    correlation N f z w + (e : ℝ) ^ 2 = radius N f e (z : ℂ) * radius N f e (w : ℂ) *
      unitCorrelation N f e z w := by
  have he : correlation N f z w + (e : ℝ) ^ 2 =
      ∑ j : Option (Deck N), (source N f e j (w : ℂ) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (source N f e j (z : ℂ))).re := by
    rw [Fintype.sum_option]
    simp only [source, ofComplex_apply, Complex.conj_ofReal, ← Complex.ofReal_mul, Complex.ofReal_re]
    change correlation N f z w + _ = (e : ℝ) * (e : ℝ) + correlation N f z w
    ring
  rw [he, unitCorrelation, Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  rw [← radius_mul_unit N f e j (w : ℂ), ← radius_mul_unit N f e j (z : ℂ)]
  simp only [map_mul, Complex.conj_ofReal, Complex.mul_re, Complex.mul_im,
    Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, zero_mul, add_zero, sub_zero,
    Complex.conj_re, Complex.conj_im]
  ring

/-- Complete augmented squared chord distance. -/
def distanceSq (z w : ℍ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j : Option (Deck N), normSq (unit N f e j (w : ℂ) - unit N f e j (z : ℂ))

private theorem normSq_sub_pair (u v : ℂ) :
    normSq (u-v) = normSq u + normSq v - 2 * (u * (starRingEnd ℂ) v).re := by
  simp only [normSq_apply, Complex.sub_re, Complex.sub_im, Complex.mul_re,
    Complex.conj_re, Complex.conj_im]
  ring

/-- Exact unit-sphere chord law, without excluding original common zeros. -/
theorem distanceSq_eq (z w : ℍ) : distanceSq N f e z w = 2 - 2 * unitCorrelation N f e z w := by
  simp only [distanceSq, normSq_sub_pair, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib,
    ← Finset.mul_sum, unit_normSq, unitCorrelation]
  ring

/-- Exact weighted chord formula retains the added-coordinate correlation correction. -/
theorem radius_mul_distanceSq (z w : ℍ) :
    radius N f e (w : ℂ) * distanceSq N f e z w =
      2 * radius N f e (w : ℂ) - 2 * (correlation N f z w + (e : ℝ) ^ 2) / radius N f e (z : ℂ) := by
  rw [distanceSq_eq, correlation_eq_radii_mul]
  field_simp [(radius_pos N f e (z : ℂ)).ne']

its exactly across an arbitrary intermediate point of a source height. -/
theorem pathResistance_add (e : Ioi (0:ℝ)) {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) (a b c : ℝ) :
    pathResistance N f e y a b+pathResistance N f e y b c=pathResistance N f e y a c := by

/-- Full retained current energy has the same exact splitting. -/
theorem pathEnergy_add (e : Ioi (0:ℝ)) {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) (a b c : ℝ) :
    pathEnergy N f e y a b+pathEnergy N f e y b c=pathEnergy N f e y a c :=
  intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals (path_energy_intervalIntegrable N f e hy a b)
    (path_energy_intervalIntegrable N f e hy b c)

/-- The complete level-period product is exactly level-width squared times the original unit-period product. -/
theorem level_period_product (e : Ioi (0:ℝ)) {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) (a : ℝ) :
    pathResistance N f e y a (a+(N+1:ℕ))*pathEnergy N f e y a (a+(N+1:ℕ))=
      ((N+1:ℕ):ℝ)^2*periodCost N f e y := by
  have hr := pathResistance_integer N f e hy a ((N+1:ℕ):ℤ)
  have he := pathEnergy_integer N f e hy a ((N+1:ℕ):ℤ)
  simp only [Int.cast_natCast,pathResistance_one_period N f e hy,pathEnergy_one_period N f e hy] at hr he
  rw [hr,he]

/-- Both arcs of the actual source loop give a uniform full-period chord comparison. -/
theorem four_chord_le_level_product (e : Ioi (0:ℝ)) {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y)
    {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hba : b < a+(N+1:ℕ)) :
    4*distanceSq N f e (ofComplex (point a y)) (ofComplex (point b y)) ≤
      ((N+1:ℕ):ℝ)^2*periodCost N f e y := by
  have h₁ := chord_le_resistance_energy N f e hy hab.le
  have h₂ := chord_le_resistance_energy N f e hy hba.le
  rw [closed_arc_distance N f e hy a b] at h₂

/-- Original regulated radii increase with the positive regulator. -/
theorem radius_mono_regulator {e r : Ioi (0:ℝ)} (he : (e:ℝ) ≤ (r:ℝ)) (z : ℂ) :
    radius N f e z ≤ radius N f r z := by
  apply Real.sqrt_le_sqrt

  change density N f (ofComplex z)+(e:ℝ)^2 ≤ density N f (ofComplex z)+(r:ℝ)^2

  refine ⟨r,2+δ,by linarith,?_⟩
  intro e he

source_arguments.statement:
theorem pow_two_pred_dvd_vacuum_of_binaryVacuumTopCellOrderLanding
    {r : ℕ} {vacuum top : ℤ} (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (h : BinaryVacuumTopCellOrderLanding r vacuum top) :
    (((2 ^ (r - 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∣ vacuum
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem pow_two_pred_dvd_vacuum_of_binaryVacuumTopCellOrderLanding
    {r : ℕ} {vacuum top : ℤ} (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (h : BinaryVacuumTopCellOrderLanding r vacuum top) :
    (((2 ^ (r - 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∣ vacuum
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  obtain ⟨cPlus, cMinus, hPlus, hMinus⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ : ∃ k, r = k + 1 := ⟨r - 1, by omega⟩
  refine ⟨cPlus + cMinus, ?_⟩
  have hTwo :
      (2 : ℤ) * (((2 ^ k : ℕ) : ℤ) * (cPlus + cMinus)) =
        (2 : ℤ) * vacuum := by
    rw [pow_succ] at hPlus hMinus
    push_cast at hPlus hMinus
    have hSum := congrArg₂ (· + ·) hPlus hMinus
    calc
      (2 : ℤ) * (((2 ^ k : ℕ) : ℤ) * (cPlus + cMinus)) =
          (((2 ^ k : ℕ) : ℤ) * 2) * cPlus +
            (((2 ^ k : ℕ) : ℤ) * 2) * cMinus := by ring
      _ = (vacuum + top) + (vacuum - top) := hSum
      _ = (2 : ℤ) * vacuum := by ring
  have hcancel := mul_left_cancel₀ (show (2 : ℤ) ≠ 0 by norm_num) hTwo
  simpa using hcancel.symm

/-- Binary cell landings at every positive rank annihilate the vacuum order even when the full
interaction order is arbitrary and rank-dependent. -/

method.description: The proof shows that 2^(r-1) divides vacuum by constructing an equality involving vacuum and using ring and cancellation operations.
steps: use ring and congrArg₂ to expand and simplify
evidence: have hcancel := mul_left_cancel₀ (show (2 : ℤ) ≠ 0 by norm_num) hTwo

# Irreducible `n`-ary law, proper-face invisibility, unbounded spectrum — Lean certification

- **ID:** ULF-IRR-1
- **Paper card:**
  `irreducible-n-ary-law-proper-face-invisibility-and-unbounded-interaction-spectrum.md`
- **Lean module:**
  `GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ConstitutiveIrreducibleInteraction`
- **Universal-law umbrella:**
  `GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.UniversalLawField`
- **Reused corpus layer:**
  `GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.NomologicalHomotopyGeometry.MinimalLawLeadingJet`
  (`MinimalLaw`, `MinimalLawEquiv`, `FirstNonzero`, `IsAbelian`, first-order invariance)

## Certified declarations

### The law

`InteractionCarrier N = (Fin N → ℝ) × ℝ` carries the `N` colours and the interaction-output line.
`interactionBracket N` is the alternating map

`ℓ_N (v₁, …, v_N) = det (Matrix.of fun i j => (v i).1 j) • z`,

built as `LinearMap.toSpanSingleton … |>.compAlternatingMap (Matrix.detRowAlternating.compLinearMap
(LinearMap.fst …))`.  `interactionBracket_colorGen` proves `ℓ_N (x₁, …, x_N) = z`, so
`interactionBracket_ne_zero` holds.  `bracketFamily N r` is the whole operation family: the bracket
in arity `N` (`bracketFamily_self`) and zero in every other arity (`bracketFamily_of_ne`), obtained
by `AlternatingMap.domDomCongr` along `finCongr`, so no dependent cast on linear maps is needed.

### Theorem 2.1 — minimality and irreducibility

`interactionBracket_fst` proves that every bracket output has zero colour component, and
`bracketFamily_eq_zero_of_fst_eq_zero` that a single colourless input annihilates the bracket.
Together they give `bracket_composite_eq_zero`: *every* composite, of any two arities and in any
slot, is zero.  Consequently `linfty_identity` proves that any signed sum of composites vanishes —
so every generalized Jacobi identity holds whatever the Koszul sign convention is, and the family
really is an `L∞` structure.  `bracketFamily_zero_and_one` records that the law is uncurved and
minimal.

`colorFace N S` is the face spanned by `z` and the colours in `S`.
`bracketFamily_comp_face_eq_zero` proves that restricting any operation to a proper face is zero: a
missing colour is an identically zero column of the defining determinant.  `faceBracketFamily` is
the corestricted face operation family, `faceLaw` the induced minimal law, and
`faceLaw_isAbelian` / `faceLaw_isAbelian_of_card_lt` prove that every face with fewer than `N`
colours is abelian.

`irreducibleLaw N hN` packages the operations as a `MinimalLaw` on `⋀[ℝ]^r (InteractionCarrier N)`.
`irreducibleLaw_not_isAbelian` proves the total law is not abelian, and `not_isAbelian_of_equiv`
transports this along any `MinimalLawEquiv`: no formal-law equivalence takes the law to an abelian
one, i.e. it is not homotopy abelian.

### Corollary 2.2 — exact interaction order

`irreducibleLaw_firstNonzero` proves `FirstNonzero N`, so the interaction order is exactly `N`.
`interactionOrder_eq` shows any equivalent law has the same first nonvanishing arity.
`arityTruncation` is the observer that discards every operation above a given arity, and
`arityTruncation_isAbelian` proves that truncating below `N` reports an abelian law.
`irreducible_properFace_invisible` bundles the four conclusions.

### Theorem 2.3 — unbounded interaction spectrum

`TowerCarrier = ∀ m : ℕ, InteractionCarrier (m + 3)` is the product of one irreducible block of
every order at least three, and `towerBracket r = AlternatingMap.pi …` is the product law.

- `towerBracket_composite_eq_zero` — the product law squares to zero;
- `towerBracket_apply_eq_zero_of_le` — an arity-`M` observer annihilates every block of order
  above `M`; `towerBracket_mem_towerHead` says all its outputs lie in the visible head;
- `zTail M` embeds the product of the output lines of all blocks of order above `M`;
  `zTail_injective`, `instInfiniteTailIndex`, and `zTail_range_disjoint_towerHead` prove the
  invisible tail is an infinite independent family meeting the visible head only at zero, and
  `towerBracket_eq_zero_of_mem_zTail` that the tail is annihilated by every arity-`M` operation;
- `not_locallyCompactSpace_pi_real` — the full interaction-output space `ℕ → ℝ` with its product
  topology is not locally compact: any neighbourhood of a point leaves some coordinate entirely
  unrestricted, so the projection of a compact neighbourhood would make `ℝ` compact.

`unbounded_interaction_spectrum` bundles these five conclusions.

## Verification

```text
lake env lean GaloisForLFunctions/HTGeometry/ConstitutiveIrreducibleInteraction.lean
lake build GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ConstitutiveIrreducibleInteraction
lake build GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.UniversalLawField
```

vanishing, the bundled irreducibility theorem, the homotopy-abelian transport, the order
invariance, the spectrum capstone, and the non-local-compactness reports only `propext`,

MUST-SOURCE-FIXED-SEPARATORS — Must specify any intermediate separator from source data before treating its energy as an ordering bound. An unspecified maximum along an unknown order gives no independent control. Must retain the signed mixed products when operations are represented by an affine family of fields. Must distinguish an ordering under predetermined endpoint values from bounds on those values: reducing a long block to its initial, separating and final energies still leaves those source energies to estimate. The [actual affine-field partition and complete subpool orders](../../3-formalized/ccm-fu-quotient-window-orders.md) are closed in Lean without numerical premises; they preserve this distinction after arbitrary retained states.


MUST-CONTROL-INHERITED-NONEMPTY-ENERGY — Must control every retained component before its squared mass exceeds the intended total budget. Cannot repair an unbounded lower bound carried by nonempty coordinates using operations that leave those coordinates unchanged, regardless of their available scalar mass. The [uniform child-source floor and scalar-reserve escape theorem](../../5-failed/ccm-fu-increasing-middle-scalar-reserves.md) certify this obstruction analytically in Lean. A surviving energy argument must change those coordinates before the obstruction forms or use another interface.

MUST-PAIR-DIRECTION-WITH-AVAILABILITY — Must prove both directional control and continued availability when corrective operations are supplied by finite source pools. A uniform spanning margin can provide a safe next move, while the smallest remaining pool limits how long that argument continues. Must account for the original squares removed by each merger: their exact cancellation with receiving squares can turn a source pairing into full-energy descent. Cannot infer complete source coverage from arbitrarily long bounded partial orders. The [actual coupled-source cone and growing prime batches](../../3-formalized/ccm-fu-coupled-prime-batches.md) establish this distinction in Lean without numerical premises.

CANNOT-FIXED-FINITE-DIRICHLET-ANNIHILATION — Cannot make one fixed nonzero finite Dirichlet polynomial vanish at every simple critical zeta zero, even after excluding any finite set of ordinates. Must retain nonvanishing at such zeros beyond every height: their unconditional superlinear census exceeds the linear zero budget of every nonzero entire function of finite exponential type. The [finite Dirichlet separation theorem](../../3-formalized/ccm-fu-finite-retained-spectral-separation.md) is closed in Lean with no computational premise. `deletionFactorizationInsertion_uniform_replication_scale`). This realizes arithmetic replication

## Exact content

## 1. Finite interaction law

Fix \(n\geq3\). Let \(V^{(n)}\) be the graded vector space with

\[
 V^{(n)}_0=\operatorname{span}\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\},
 \qquad
 V^{(n)}_{2-n}=kz,
\tag{IL.1}
\]

and no other components. Define an uncurved \(L_\infty\) structure by

\[
 \ell_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=z
\tag{IL.2}
\]

with graded antisymmetric extension, and set every other bracket to zero. Also set \(\ell_n=0\)
whenever one input is \(z\).

Each generator \(x_i\) is called a color. For \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the \(S\)-face is the
subspace spanned by \(z\) and the \(x_i\) with \(i\in S\), with the restricted brackets.

## 2. Theorem

### Theorem 2.1 — irreducible proper-face-invisible law

The operations above define a minimal \(L_\infty\) algebra. Every proper color-face
\(S\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is abelian, while the total \(L_\infty\) algebra is not homotopy
abelian.

Thus:

\[
 \boxed{
 \text{every proper observer face is law-trivial}
 \quad\centernot\Longrightarrow\quad
 \text{the total law is trivial}.}
\tag{IL.3}
\]

The first nonzero minimal operation has arity \(n\) and is exactly (IL.2). Its structured
conjugacy class is invariant under \(L_\infty\) equivalence.

### Corollary 2.2 — exact interaction order

Define the interaction order of a minimal law \(Q\) by

\[
 \iota(Q)=\inf\{r\geq2:\ell_r\neq0\}.
\tag{IL.4}
\]

Then

\[
 \iota(V^{(n)})=n.
\tag{IL.5}
\]

Every observer retaining fewer than \(n\) colors or truncating operations below arity \(n\)
reports an abelian law.

### Theorem 2.3 — unbounded interaction spectrum

Let

\[
 V_\infty=\prod_{n\geq3}V^{(n)}
\tag{IL.6}
\]

with the product filtration, and let \(Q_\infty\) be the product of the brackets (IL.2). Then:

1. \(Q_\infty^2=0\);
2. for every \(N\), the arity-\(N\) observer kills all interactions of orders \(n>N\);
3. the invisible tail contains
   \[
   \prod_{n>N}kz_n;
   \tag{IL.7}
   \]
4. over \(k=\mathbb R\), the product topology on the full interaction-output space
   \(\prod_{n\geq3}\mathbb Rz_n\) is not locally compact.

Hence unbounded interaction order supplies a noncompact source of observer escape that is distinct
from curvature, orbit density, and ordinary infinite-dimensional tangent rank.

## 3. Proof

The only potentially nonzero \(L_\infty\) identity is a composite in which one copy of
\(\ell_n\) is inserted into another. The inner operation outputs \(z\), while every operation with
a \(z\)-input was defined to vanish. Therefore every composite is zero and all \(L_\infty\)
identities hold. Since \(\ell_1=0\), the law is minimal.

A proper color-face omits at least one of the required inputs in (IL.2), so every restricted
bracket vanishes. On the total space, (IL.2) is nonzero. A minimal \(L_\infty\) algebra
quasi-isomorphic to an abelian one is isomorphic to the zero minimal structure; equivalently, an
invertible linear term conjugates the first nonzero minimal operation and cannot annihilate it.
Thus the total law is not homotopy abelian.

The product law squares to zero componentwise. Arity truncation at \(N\) removes every
\(\ell_n\) with \(n>N\), proving (IL.7). An infinite product of nonzero finite-dimensional real
vector spaces is not locally compact: every basic neighborhood leaves infinitely many unrestricted
coordinates and has no compact closure.

## 4. Contextuality versus interaction

The connected-parity contextual model and Theorem 2.1 have identical proper-face blindness but
opposite global ontologies:

- **contextuality:** no global deterministic law exists;
- **irreducible interaction:** a global law exists, but it is a genuinely higher operation.

Therefore proper-face blindness alone cannot decide whether the universal object is
nonclassical-without-points or higher-interacting-with-points. Any universal field must retain this
distinction.

## 5. Operadic interpretation

The law (IL.2) is an algebra over the \(L_\infty\) operad with one irreducible \(n\)-ary generator.
Equivalently, it is a Maurer--Cartan coderivation supported in arity \(n\). Its proper color
restrictions kill the twisting morphism, while the total color set retains it.

This makes law generation operadic:

- colors are observer types;
- the twisting morphism is the sourced interaction;
- proper-face formality is restriction of colors;
- unbounded arity is an infinite bar/cobar interaction tower.

`Type`) with the appropriate `Comm*` instance. However, in other cases, the commutativity of the
subobject may be conditional on commutativity of some other object. For example,
`Subgroup.closure s` is not always commutative, but it is when `s` is a commutative subset.
Likewise, if `S : Subgroup G` is a commutative subgroup, then `S.topologicalClosure` is also
commutative.

For such scenarios, users should prefer to use the unbundled `IsMulCommutative` typeclass, and to
provide theorems such as:
```
theorem isMulCommutative_closure {G : Type*} [Group G] {k : Set G}
    (hcomm : ∀ x ∈ k, ∀ y ∈ k, x * y = y * x) :
    IsMulCommutative (closure k)
```
or even *instances* such as
```
instance Subgroup.instIsMulCommutative_closure {S G : Type*} [Group G] [SetLike S G]
    [MulMemClass S G] (s : S) [IsMulCommutative s] :
    IsMulCommutative (closure (s : Set G))
```
and
```
instance Subgroup.isMulCommutative_topologicalClosure [T2Space G] (s : Subgroup G)
    [IsMulCommutative s] : IsMulCommutative s.topologicalClosure
```
Note that we prefer to name these instances manually because they are occasionally useful as
theorems. For example, the proof of the topological closure instance for subgroups above is proved
immediately from the one for monoids via: `s.toSubmonoid.isMulCommutative_topologicalClosure`.

In practice, we wish to be able to use the library of theorems about (bundled) commutativity for
subobjects as well, and so we also provide instances which take as input the unbundled
`Group G` and `IsMulCommutative G` and produce the bundled `CommGroup G`. However, to avoid
deleterious effects to type class synthesis for bundled commutativity (by forcing Lean to search
the entirery of both the bundled and unbundled hierarchies), these instances are only
available inside the `IsMulCommutative` scope and are simultaneously given the very low priority
`50`.
-/

import Mathlib.GroupTheory.GroupAction.Basic

/-!
# A free action commuting with a transitive abelian action is abelian
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

variable {P G M : Type*} [Group G] [Group M] [MulAction G P] [MulAction M P]

/-- **Transport of commutativity across two commuting actions.**  If `G` has an injective orbit map
at `x₀`, if `M` reaches every point from `x₀`, and if the two actions commute elementwise, then
commutativity of `M` forces commutativity of `G`.

This is the deck-group/monodromy comparison: for a connected covering the deck group acts with
injective orbit map, the monodromy acts transitively, the two commute, and the monodromy of a
covering of a topological group is abelian. -/
theorem mul_comm_of_commuting_transitive_of_mul_comm (x₀ : P)
    (hfree : ∀ g h : G, g • x₀ = h • x₀ → g = h)
    (htrans : ∀ y : P, ∃ μ : M, μ • x₀ = y)
    (hcomm : ∀ (g : G) (μ : M) (x : P), μ • (g • x) = g • (μ • x))
    (hab : ∀ μ ν : M, μ * ν = ν * μ) (g h : G) :
    g * h = h * g := by
  obtain ⟨μg, hμg⟩ := htrans (g • x₀)
  obtain ⟨μh, hμh⟩ := htrans (h • x₀)
  refine hfree _ _ ?_
  have e1 : (μg * μh) • x₀ = (h * g) • x₀ := by
    rw [mul_smul, hμh, hcomm, hμg, ← mul_smul]
  have e2 : (μh * μg) • x₀ = (g * h) • x₀ := by
    rw [mul_smul, hμg, hcomm, hμh, ← mul_smul]
  rw [← e2, ← e1, hab]

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

public import Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Arithmetic

/-!
# Ordinal arithmetic commutativity

Results on the commutativity of ordinal arithmetic operations.

## References

* [Wacław Sierpiński, *Cardinal and Ordinal Numbers*][sierpinski1958]
-/

public section

namespace Ordinal

theorem addCommute_iff_eq_mul_natCast {o₁ o₂ : Ordinal} :
    AddCommute o₁ o₂ ↔ ∃ (o : Ordinal) (n₁ n₂ : ℕ), o * n₁ = o₁ ∧ o * n₂ = o₂ := by
  refine ⟨fun hcomm ↦ ?_, ?_⟩
  · induction h : o₁ + o₂ using WellFoundedLT.induction generalizing o₁ o₂ with | ind o ih
    subst h
    wlog hle : o₁ ≤ o₂
    · grind [hcomm.symm]
    rcases eq_or_ne o₁ 0 with (rfl | h₁)
    · exact ⟨o₂, 0, 1, by simp, by simp⟩
    let o₃ := o₂ - o₁
    have hsub : o₁ + o₃ = o₂ := Ordinal.add_sub_cancel_of_le hle
    have hcomm' : AddCommute o₁ o₃ := add_left_cancel (a := o₁) <| by grind
    have hlt : o₁ + o₃ < o₁ + o₂ := by simpa [hsub, hcomm.eq] using h₁.pos
    rcases ih _ hlt hcomm' rfl with ⟨o, n₁, n₃, hn₁, hn₃⟩
    use o, n₁, n₁ + n₃, hn₁
    rw [Nat.cast_add, mul_add, hn₁, hn₃, hsub]
  · rintro ⟨o, n₁, n₂, rfl, rfl⟩
    rw [addCommute_iff_eq, ← mul_add, ← mul_add, ← Nat.cast_add, add_comm, Nat.cast_add]

end Ordinal

          ∫ t in u..(u + T),
            ((periodicProductFejerTent N ρ c (fun j => t * ω j) : ℝ) : ℂ))
          - (((ρ / (2 * π)) ^ d : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
        (2 * C / T) * periodicFejerMultiplicativeCost N ρ c eps

by
  classical
  set S := nonconstantPacketIndexSet N d with hS
  obtain ⟨C, hC, hpacket⟩ :=
    KleinbockMargulis.exists_global_indexedFourierPacketHaarDiscrepancy
      (ι := {k // k ∈ S}) hω heps
  refine ⟨C, hC, ?_⟩
  intro u T hT
  have hpoint : ∀ t : ℝ,
      ((periodicProductFejerTent N ρ c (fun j => t * ω j) : ℝ) : ℂ) =
        (((ρ / (2 * π)) ^ d : ℝ) : ℂ)
          + ∑ i : {k // k ∈ S}, packetAmp N ρ c i.1 *
            Complex.exp ((t : ℂ) *
              (KleinbockMargulis.dotProd (packetCharacter i.1) ω : ℂ) *
                Complex.I) := by
    intro t
    rw [periodicProductFejerTent_eq_const_add N hρ hρπ]
    change (((ρ / (2 * π)) ^ d : ℝ) : ℂ) +
        ∑ k ∈ nonconstantPacketIndexSet N d,
          packetMode N ρ c (fun j => t * ω j) k = _
    rw [← hS]
    congr 1
    rw [Finset.sum_coe_sort S (fun k => packetAmp N ρ c k *
      Complex.exp ((t : ℂ) *
        (KleinbockMargulis.dotProd (packetCharacter k) ω : ℂ) * Complex.I))]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => by
      rw [packetMode_linearPhase N ρ c ω k t,
        dotProd_packetCharacter]
  have hmain := hpacket
    (((ρ / (2 * π)) ^ d : ℝ) : ℂ)
    (fun i : {k // k ∈ S} => packetAmp N ρ c i.1)
    (fun i : {k // k ∈ S} => packetCharacter i.1)
    (fun i => by
      apply packetCharacter_ne_zero_of_mem_nonconstantPacketIndexSet
      rw [← hS]
      exact i.2) u T hT
  rw [show periodicFejerMultiplicativeCost N ρ c eps =
      KleinbockMargulis.indexedMultiplicativeFourierL1Cost
        (ι := {k // k ∈ S})
        (fun i => packetAmp N ρ c i.1)
        (fun i => packetCharacter i.1) eps by rfl]
  have hInt :
      (∫ t in u..(u + T),
        ((periodicProductFejerTent N ρ c (fun j => t * ω j) : ℝ) : ℂ)) =
      ∫ t in u..(u + T),
        ((((ρ / (2 * π)) ^ d : ℝ) : ℂ)
          + ∑ i : {k // k ∈ S}, packetAmp N ρ c i.1 *
            Complex.exp ((t : ℂ) *
              (KleinbockMargulis.dotProd (packetCharacter i.1) ω : ℂ) *
                Complex.I)) :=
    intervalIntegral.integral_congr fun t _ => hpoint t
  rw [hInt]
  exact hmain

# CCM quantile characteristic-transport law

- **ID:** ccm-quantile-characteristic-transport-law
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM
- **Source:** `CCMActualHeadOutgoingQuantileCharacteristicTransport.lean`
- **Statement:** The finite outgoing-quantile phase symbol is exactly the cosine-characteristic
  discrepancy between continuous outgoing polar mass on `[0,b_N]` and atomic prime mass at
  `log n`, coupled cellwise by equal mass; its curvature telescopes to the corresponding global
  second-moment discrepancy.

## Goal

Replace cellwise phase bookkeeping by one transported Fourier--Stieltjes source without losing the
monotone quantile coupling. This exposes transport cost and moment structure to Hilbert-space
positivity tools. It is a bridge theorem, not an RH proof.

## Gates

- [x] 0 → 1 in-progress: exact source definitions and proof route identified; corpus search found
  no aggregate characteristic-discrepancy theorem
- [x] 1 → 2 fully-proven: complete paper proof, `[PROVED HERE]`, no open dependency
- [x] 2 → 3 formalized: nine Lean theorems, targeted source/build/axiom audit
- [ ] 3 → 4 publication-ready: standalone proof and external novelty audit

## Theorem A — characteristic discrepancy `[PROVED HERE]`

For `b_N = ccmOutgoingPrimeQuantileBoundary N` and frequency `xi`,

`Q_N(xi) = ∫_[0,b_N] exp(h/2) cos(2*pi*h*xi) dh
  - sum_(n<N) w_n cos(2*pi*log(n)*xi)`.

This is not the ordinary same-window prime cutoff: atomic nodes retain quantile transport order and
may lie outside their polar cell. It is the characteristic discrepancy of the explicit coupling.

## Theorem B — global curvature `[PROVED HERE]`

`Q_N''(0) = 4*pi^2 * (
  sum_(n<N) w_n*(log n)^2 - ∫_[0,b_N] exp(h/2)*h^2 dh)`.

The right side is the second-moment difference of the two equal-mass finite measures.

## Theorem C — quadratic transport bound `[PROVED HERE]`

Define the literal absolute second-moment work

`A_N = sum_(n<N) ∫_[b_n,b_(n+1)] exp(h/2) * |h^2 - (log n)^2| dh`.

Then

`|Q_N(xi)| ≤ (2*pi*xi)^2/2 * A_N`.

The proof uses the new global inequality

`|cos x - cos y| ≤ |x^2-y^2|/2`,

obtained from the exact product formula for `cos x - cos y` and `|sin u| ≤ |u|`. This is stronger
at low frequency than a generic Lipschitz bound. It formalizes a useful separation: signed
second-moment work determines curvature, while absolute second-moment work controls magnitude.

## Approach

1. Use exact quantile cell mass to split each profile into polar cosine mass minus atom cosine mass.
2. Induct over consecutive boundaries to telescope continuous cell integrals.
3. Differentiate the finite sum using already proved cell jets and telescope second moments.
4. Compare the characteristic discrepancy with `HTGeometry.QuantileCoupling` and
   `HTGeometry.QuadraticTransportCost`; import them only if a theorem uses their measure-level API.

All four steps are closed. Measure-level imports were not needed: the corpus's literal cell
coupling supports a sharper direct quadratic estimate.

## Hostile audit

- Equal mass gives `Q_N(0)=0` but no pointwise sign.
- Second-moment difference is signed and is not quadratic transport cost.
- Atomic support is indexed by transport cells, not clipped by `log n ≤ b_N`.
- Any bound must retain frequency scaling and cannot replace exact phase identity by absolute mass.

## Novelty audit

- Internal research search found general monotone-coupling and quadratic-cost theorems plus the new
  cell phase module, but no theorem identifying this CCM finite symbol with a transported
  characteristic discrepancy.
- Labels: `[BRIDGE] [INTERNAL CANDIDATE] [NOT AN RH PROOF]`.

## Lean formalization

Module: `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/CCMActualHeadOutgoingQuantileCharacteristicTransport.lean`

- exact consecutive-cell telescope to `[0,b_N]`
- exact cell polar-minus-atom characteristic identity
- exact finite characteristic-discrepancy identity

## Question

After adaptive-width regularization is retired, what exact classical arithmetic object carries
the fixed-ratio FCRJ energy burden? Can the positive prime-pair tent be recentered without losing
physical coefficients, clipping, or source orientation?

## Answer

For finite physical packet `P`, define cumulative prime-log mass and unit-density discrepancy

```text
C_P(t) = sum_(p in P, log p <= t) log(p)/p,
D_P(t) = C_P(t)-t.
```

The raw moving flux has exact coboundary decomposition

```text
Flux_P(m,k;u)
 = C_P(k-u)-C_P(m-u)
 = (k-m)+D_P(k-u)-D_P(m-u).                            (MC1)
```

Let `L_P` be physical weighted clipped-length mass. Exact aperture centering gives

```text
CenteredFlux_P(A,m,k;u)
 = [D_P(k-u)-D_P(m-u)]-[L_P/A-(k-m)].                  (MC2)
```

The scalar centered flux is almost everywhere the concrete complex Hilbert carrier already used
by FCRJ. Therefore

```text
Energy_P(A,m,k)
 = integral_0^A |CenteredFlux_P(A,m,k;u)|^2 du
 = integral_0^A
     |D_P(k-u)-D_P(m-u)-[L_P/A-(k-m)]|^2 du.           (MC3)
```

At fixed physical scale `X` and ratio width `c`, put `m=log X`, `k=log X+c`. Then

```text
Energy_P(A,log X,log X+c) <= B

iff

integral_0^A
  |D_P(log X+c-u)-D_P(log X-u)-[L_P/A-c]|^2 du <= B.   (MC4)
```

/-- **Sharp elementary capacity window.** -/
theorem capacity_window {a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) (A : Set S) :
    (1 - a) * C.statMeasure A ≤ C.capacity a A ∧
      C.capacity a A ≤ C.statMeasure A ∧ C.capacity a A ≤ 1 - a := by
  classical
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [(C.capacity_eq ha0 ha1 A).2]
    refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ => ?_) (by linarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1 - a)
    by_cases hx : x ∈ A
    · rw [Set.indicator_of_mem hx, C.potential_of_mem a hx, mul_one]
    · rw [Set.indicator_of_notMem hx]
      exact mul_nonneg (C.stat_pos x).le (C.potential_nonneg a A x)
  · have hle := C.energy_potential_le ha0 ha1
      (f := Set.indicator A (1 : S → ℝ)) (fun x hx => by rw [Set.indicator_of_mem hx]; rfl)
    refine le_trans hle (le_of_le_of_eq ?_ (C.inner_indicator_self A))
    rw [energy, energyBil, inner_killed_expand]
    have := mul_nonneg ha0 (C.inner_indicator_nonneg A)
    linarith
  · have hle := C.energy_potential_le ha0 ha1 (A := A) (f := (1 : S → ℝ)) (fun x _ => rfl)
    refine le_trans hle (le_of_eq ?_)
    rw [energy, energyBil, C.killed_one, C.inner_smul_right, C.inner_one_left]
    simp [C.stat_sum]

/-- **Stationary first-entrance mean.**  The stationary mean of the equilibrium potential is the
capacity divided by the killing rate. -/
theorem stationary_mean {a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a < 1) (A : Set S) :
    ∑ x, C.stat x * C.potential a A x = C.capacity a A / (1 - a) := by
  have h := (C.capacity_eq ha0 ha1.le A).2
  have hpos : (0:ℝ) < 1 - a := by linarith
  rw [h, mul_comm, mul_div_assoc, div_self hpos.ne', mul_one]

/-- The stationary first-entrance mass differs from the target volume by at most the killing
factor. -/
theorem statMeasure_le_stationary_mean {a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a < 1) (A : Set S) :
    C.statMeasure A ≤ ∑ x, C.stat x * C.potential a A x ∧
      ∑ x, C.stat x * C.potential a A x ≤ C.statMeasure A / (1 - a) := by
  have hwin := C.capacity_window ha0 ha1.le A
  have hmean := C.stationary_mean ha0 ha1 A
  have hpos : (0:ℝ) < 1 - a := by linarith
  constructor
  · rw [hmean, le_div_iff₀ hpos]
    have := hwin.1
    linarith
  · rw [hmean, div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hpos]
    exact hwin.2.1

/-- The density of a law against the stationary law. -/
noncomputable def density (ν : S → ℝ) : S → ℝ := fun x => ν x / C.stat x

theorem stat_mul_density (ν : S → ℝ) (x : S) : C.stat x * C.density ν x = ν x := by
  rw [density, mul_div_cancel₀ _ (C.stat_pos x).ne']

/-- The directional capacity discrepancy of a law. -/
noncomputable def discrepancy (a : ℝ) (A : Set S) (ν : S → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  C.inner (C.density ν - 1) (C.potential a A)

/-- The chi-square divergence of a law against the stationary law. -/
noncomputable def chiSq (ν : S → ℝ) : ℝ := C.inner (C.density ν - 1) (C.density ν - 1)

/-- The killed negative-energy square of a law against the stationary law. -/
noncomputable def dualNormSq (a : ℝ) (ν : S → ℝ) : ℝ := C.negEnergySq a (C.density ν - 1)

/-- **Capacity--discrepancy law.**  The mean first-entrance mass of a law is the stationary mean
plus its directional capacity discrepancy. -/
theorem mean_potential_eq {a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a < 1) (A : Set S) (ν : S → ℝ) :
    ∑ x, ν x * C.potential a A x =
      C.capacity a A / (1 - a) + C.discrepancy a A ν := by
  have hterm : ∀ x : S, C.stat x * ((C.density ν - 1) x * C.potential a A x) =
      ν x * C.potential a A x - C.stat x * C.potential a A x := by
    intro x
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply, Pi.one_apply]
    have h := C.stat_mul_density ν x
    linear_combination (C.potential a A x) * h
  rw [discrepancy, inner, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => hterm x, Finset.sum_sub_distrib,
    ← C.stationary_mean ha0 ha1 A]
  ring

/-- **Directional discrepancy bound.**  The directional discrepancy is controlled by capacity and
the killed negative-energy square. -/
theorem abs_discrepancy_le {a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a < 1) (A : Set S) (ν : S → ℝ) :
    |C.discrepancy a A ν| ≤ Real.sqrt (C.capacity a A) * Real.sqrt (C.dualNormSq a ν) := by
  have hcs := C.inner_sq_le_energy_mul_negEnergySq ha0 ha1 (C.density ν - 1) (C.potential a A)
  have hsq : (C.discrepancy a A ν) ^ 2 ≤ C.capacity a A * C.dualNormSq a ν := by
    rw [discrepancy, capacity, dualNormSq, mul_comm]
    exact hcs
  have hnn : 0 ≤ C.capacity a A * C.dualNormSq a ν :=
    le_trans (sq_nonneg _) hsq
  have hcap : (0:ℝ) ≤ C.capacity a A := C.energy_nonneg ha0 ha1.le _
  have hle := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hsq
  rwa [Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs, Real.sqrt_mul hcap] at hle

/-- **Global discrepancy obstruction.**  The killed negative-energy square dominates the
chi-square divergence up to the killed spectral radius. -/
